title: The Tinker Table
strapline: Real screwdrivers, real screws, a broken radio to take apart — the deep satisfaction of finding out how.
intent: Children investigate how things work by taking real objects apart, feeding a powerful curiosity about mechanisms.
Children use real tools — screwdrivers, spanners, pliers — with control, care and growing competence.
Children solve practical problems: how does this come apart, what does this part do, how do I undo it.
Children develop strength, dexterity and hand-eye coordination through genuine, purposeful work.
Children build confidence, focus and a sense of being trusted with real, grown-up tools.
implementation: Provide safe, disassemble-able objects — an old radio, a clock, a telephone, a keyboard — batteries and sharp parts removed first.
Offer real child-sized tools: screwdrivers, spanners, pliers, and a tray to keep the removed parts.
Teach and model tool safety and technique explicitly before children start, and supervise closely.
Let children lead the investigation — undoing, exploring, sorting parts — without a required outcome.
Feed in the language of mechanism: screw, unscrew, turn, tight, loose, part, inside, connect.
Talk about what parts might do and how they fit together, following the child's wonder.
Keep a 'parts library' of the interesting bits for building and further tinkering.
key_questions: How do you think this comes apart?
Which tool would help you undo that?
What do you think this part does?
Which way do you turn the screwdriver to loosen it?
How does it all fit together inside?

impact.text: Children investigate how real objects work by taking them apart.
Children use real tools with control and care.
Children develop hand strength and dexterity.
Children use the language of mechanism and how things fit.
Children concentrate deeply and feel trusted with real work.

enhancements: A rotating supply of safe objects to dismantle — old tech, wind-up toys.
A parts library of interesting bits for building afterwards.
A real workbench with a vice at child height.
Nuts, bolts and jar lids for twisting and threading practice.
Magnifiers to look closely at the parts inside.
A tinkering logbook to draw what was found inside.

playing_exploring: Children explore how real things work with hands-on curiosity.
They open, undo and investigate to find out.
active_learning: Children concentrate for long stretches on a fiddly take-apart.
They persist to loosen a stubborn screw or free a part.
creating_thinking: Children work out how something comes apart and what parts do.
They choose the right tool and technique for each job.
